title: No evidence that physical forces give way to unknown vital agencies in development

fields.label: Label
fields.value: No evidence that physical forces give way to unknown vital agencies in development

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although forces other than surface tension act in a growing embryo, there is no evidence at any stage that physical forces cease to govern its material form and are replaced by agencies unknown to physics.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But we have no evidence whatsoever that at this point, or that point, or at any, the dominion of the physical forces over the material system gives place to a new condition where agencies at present unknown to the physicist impose themselves on the living matter

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Physical forces versus vital agencies”. Scope: developing embryos and living tissues generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-16: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.07

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a conceptual rejection of vitalism rather than a bounded empirical model. Because the alternative is undefined and physical forces necessarily act on material tissue, no outcome in an existing dataset uniquely resolves it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No dataset can distinguish universal physical governance from replacement by an undefined agency unknown to physics without an independent measurable prediction for that agency.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The rival 'unknown vital agency' has no measurable definition.

The assertion is framed as absence of evidence over all development.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a conceptual denial that vital agencies replace physical ones, not a statement with a measurable residue. Developmental image archives contain forms and genes and forces, and none of those variables marks the boundary the claim denies. Every empirical outcome can be read as still physical, so the claim cannot be confirmed or refuted by existing data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim asserts that no stage of development shows physical forces giving way to agencies outside physics. Any unexplained embryonic pattern is compatible both with physics not yet identified and with a vital agency, so no public measurement distinguishes the two.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Failure to find a non-physical residue is not a confirming result under this wording.

An agency unknown to physics has no separate observable that a dataset could record.
